prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.


SUBJECT-SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS:
Draw ONLY the nearest entrance gate building in photo 2: the 1735 Shanmen of Guandi Temple in Zhoukou, Henan 周口关帝庙山门. In the aerial photograph it is the complete large green roof and gray/red facade in the foreground, NOT the deeper courtyard halls, stone archway or theater. Translate this fully visible gate into an almost straight-on facade with minimal visible side, preserve its actual low wide proportions. One single hipped-gable xieshan roof with one eave level, exactly FIVE facade bays: a large central rectangular open passage, one red double-leaf doorway on either side (three doorways total), and a closed gray-wall bay at each extreme containing one small CIRCULAR window. Thus two round windows total. Keep plain round window surrounds and door frames, outline door studs only very sparingly. Actual green glazed ridge ornament has a small central upright finial and elaborate end ornaments, retain those silhouettes simply. Keep its modest stepped stone platform and short central steps. Remove trees, ticket signs, barriers, people, stone lions, flagpoles and ALL neighboring or rear buildings. No lettering or plaque text. Roof surfaces remain entirely white with only 5 or 6 short indicative tile strokes near an edge; no repetitive tiling. White walls without brick grid. Entire single gate uncropped with generous 10 percent margin, landscape 1536x1024.

site_recommendation.name: 周口关帝庙
site_recommendation.yearNote: 取所绘山门建造年 1735；不使用会馆整体始建于 1693 或全部落成于 1852 的纪年替代。
site_recommendation.place: 河南 · 周口市川汇区
site_recommendation.lede: 三道门洞与两侧圆窗，收在一座五间歇山顶下。山门之后，是山陕商人在周家口持续营建的会馆院落。

facts.label: 所绘山门
facts.text: 山门建于清雍正十三年（1735），面阔五间、进深三间，单檐歇山顶。

facts.label: 会馆沿革
facts.text: 建筑群由山西、陕西旅周商人集资兴建，始建于 1693 年，后经多朝扩建与重修。

facts.label: 构图依据
facts.text: 依据周口市政府公布的航拍正面取最前部山门，保留三门两圆窗；不把后院飨殿、戏楼叠入单体。
